core.title: Zero-Shot Open Circuit Fault Diagnosis of Converter Based on Prior-Knowledge Injected Dual Bayesian Network With Attention Mechanism
core.venue: IEEE transactions on industrial electronics (1982. Print)
core.abstract: Power electronic systems serve as core infrastructure for modern energy conversion and power control. Their reliability is crucial for the stable operation of key fields, such as industrial power systems, transportation, and aerospace. Open-circuit faults are difficult to detect, which can lead to serious consequences. While effective in data-rich environments, existing data-driven approaches’ reliance on extensive labeled data hinders their practical deployment. The reason is that acquiring comprehensive fault data in real-world settings is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, this article proposes a dual Bayesian zero-shot fault diagnosis approach based on prior-knowledge injected with attention mechanism (PKIDBAAM). This approach constructs a fault attribute space with clear physical meaning by analyzing the physical relationship between the Vienna rectifier topology and fault modes. It employs a multihead attention mechanism to dynamically fuse multidomain fault features from three-phase current signals. A dual Bayesian inference framework combining naive Bayes and integrated multiple Gaussian Bayesian algorithms is designed to achieve high accuracy recognition of inaccessible open-circuit faults. The verification results on a Vienna rectifier experimental platform show that it significantly outperforms conventional classical machine learning models, which provides a new solution for intelligent fault diagnosis in power electronic systems.
core.summary: 本文针对变换器开路故障难检测、完整标注故障数据获取成本高的问题，提出先验知识注入与注意力机制结合的双贝叶斯零样本诊断方法。其利用Vienna整流器拓扑与故障模式的物理关系构建属性空间，以多头注意力融合三相电流的多域特征，再通过双贝叶斯推断识别难以获取数据的故障。摘要报告实验平台验证优于传统机器学习模型，但未给出定量指标与零样本划分。本导读仅依据摘要，不代表全文评审。[摘要]

raw_metadata.recommendation: 建议重点关注物理故障属性如何连接已知与未见故障，以及双贝叶斯推断的具体实现；这与少标签智能运维直接相关，但推荐强度仍需全文中的数据划分、对照与消融证据支撑。[摘要]

deep_read.problem: 研究针对开路故障难检测与故障标注数据难获取的双重问题。摘要指出既有数据驱动方法存在“reliance on extensive labeled data”，全面获取故障数据往往成本过高。核心问题因此是如何利用可得信号与先验知识，识别缺乏可获取样本的故障，而非仅提高数据充足时的分类表现。[摘要]
deep_read.method: 方法先分析Vienna整流器拓扑与故障模式的物理关系，建立故障属性空间；再以“multihead attention mechanism”融合三相电流的多域特征；最后结合朴素贝叶斯与集成多高斯贝叶斯算法形成双贝叶斯推断框架。摘要未交代属性编码、训练目标与各模块的具体连接方式。[摘要]
deep_read.innovation: 摘要可确认的方法特色是将物理属性空间、注意力特征融合与双贝叶斯推断组合用于零样本诊断，其中属性空间具有“clear physical meaning”。解读：潜在价值在于让物理知识参与未见故障识别，而非仅增加分类模块；但其相对既有零样本方法的原创程度，尚无充分对照信息可判定。[摘要]
deep_read.findings: 摘要报告在Vienna整流器实验平台进行了验证，并称该方法“significantly outperforms conventional classical machine learning models”。这支持作者报告了比较优势，但未提供准确率、误报率、重复试验或统计检验信息，不能据此量化提升幅度，也不能确认优势覆盖哪些未见故障与运行工况。[摘要]
deep_read.limitations: 当前限制首先是资料范围仅为摘要，而非已证实的方法缺陷。摘要使用“inaccessible open-circuit faults”描述识别对象，却未说明不可获取的具体含义及训练测试划分；同时缺少样本规模、基线配置和消融结果。因此无法判断零样本设置的严格性、模块贡献与跨工况泛化能力。[摘要]
deep_read.connection: 解读：该研究与智能运维直接相关，因为它面向故障样本稀缺下的自动诊断；与可靠性研究的联系在于为故障识别提供技术支持，摘要以“Their reliability is crucial”交代背景，但并未开展寿命或失效概率建模。拓扑知识在此用于诊断属性构建，不能将其视为结构设计优化成果。[摘要]
deep_read.next_steps: 建议：阅读全文时优先核查故障属性的物理定义、未见类别划分及先验知识是否涉及测试信息；随后检查注意力与双贝叶斯模块的独立消融、基线公平性和工况变化测试。若用于自身运维研究，可再设计噪声与负载扰动验证。这些是后续核验和迁移建议，不是摘要已报告的实验。[摘要]

article.lead: 真实设备的开路故障数据昂贵且难以收集，依赖大量标注样本的诊断方法因此面临落地障碍。这项研究以Vienna整流器为对象，将物理先验、注意力机制与双贝叶斯推断结合，探索对难以获取数据的开路故障进行零样本诊断。

sections.title: 故障难采集，诊断不能只靠堆数据
paragraphs: 电力电子系统承担能量转换与功率控制，其可靠性关系到工业电力系统、交通运输和航空航天等领域的稳定运行。开路故障难以检测，而实际场景中获取全面故障数据的成本又很高，这使依赖大量标注数据的方法受到限制。
本文关注的核心问题是：当目标开路故障的数据难以获得时，能否利用电路自身的物理关系辅助识别，而不是完全依赖故障样本覆盖？摘要提出的零样本诊断方法，正是围绕这一数据瓶颈展开。

sections.title: 把物理属性、电流特征与贝叶斯推断结合
paragraphs: 作者提出融合先验知识与注意力机制的双贝叶斯零样本故障诊断方法，简称PKIDBAAM。方法首先分析Vienna整流器拓扑与故障模式之间的物理关系，据此构建具有明确物理意义的故障属性空间。
在信号侧，方法采用多头注意力机制，动态融合来自三相电流信号的多域故障特征；在推断侧，将朴素贝叶斯与集成多高斯贝叶斯算法结合，构成双贝叶斯推断框架，用于识别难以获取数据的开路故障。

sections.title: 实验平台报告优于经典机器学习模型
paragraphs: 摘要报告，研究在Vienna整流器实验平台上进行了验证，结果显著优于常规经典机器学习模型。这为所提方法在该平台上的故障诊断能力提供了支持，但摘要没有给出准确率、性能差值或具体对比模型，不能据此量化优势大小。

sections.title: 零样本划分与验证边界仍需查阅正文
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断实验样本规模、故障类别覆盖、已见与未见故障的划分，以及训练和测试数据如何组织；也无法核对比较模型的配置、评价指标与“显著优于”的统计依据。这些属于当前资料未报告的信息，不意味着论文没有开展相应工作。
摘要明确提到的验证对象是Vienna整流器实验平台，尚不足以判断方法在其他变换器拓扑、不同运行工况或实际部署环境中的适用范围，也不能把潜在的智能运维价值视为已经验证的工程效果。

sections.title: 阅读启发：关注物理属性如何连接未见故障
paragraphs: 阅读启发：这项工作的值得关注之处，是把具有物理意义的故障属性引入数据受限的诊断问题。进一步阅读时，可重点追问属性空间如何连接已见与未见故障、多头注意力与双贝叶斯推断各自发挥什么作用，以及实验如何界定零样本识别。厘清这些问题，比仅关注总体性能更有助于判断其智能运维价值。

core.title: Predicting crack initiation in highly deformed rail steel; Plasticity modeling, machine-learning-accelerated plasticity simulations, and fatigue criteria
core.abstract: Rolling Contact Fatigue (RCF) crack initiation, causing major problems for the railway industry, is often associated with large plastic deformations accumulated in the surface layer of rails and wheels. These deformations are known to affect the mechanical and fatigue behavior of the material and to induce anisotropy. Even so, many RCF crack initiation studies do not account for the influence of the deformed near-surface material. Moreover, numerical simulations of the long-term accumulation of plastic deformations under traffic loading are computationally demanding. To address these challenges, the goal of this thesis is to develop methodologies for both more accurate predictions of RCF crack initiation in the highly deformed near-surface rail material and computationally efficient modeling of plasticity.In the first part of the thesis, a framework is developed for predicting RCF crack initiation in railheads subjected to mixed traffic loading, with a focus on the effects of the highly deformed rail surface layer and profile geometry changes. In particular, an anisotropic material model is calibrated against experiments with railway-like loading at different material states, corresponding to different depths in the railhead. The identified material parameters are then used to consider spatially varying properties in the railhead, governed by an accumulated shear strain distribution reconstructed from measurements in field samples. The framework further incorporates an improved crack initiation criterion that accounts for the accumulated plastic deformations. The findings underline the significant importance of accounting for the deformed near-surface material and rail profile geometry changes when predicting RCF crack initiation.The second part of the thesis presents two approaches to reducing the computational cost of cyclic plasticity simulations. First, a cycle-domain material model is used to predict peak stress and plastic strain in each loading cycle. Machine Learning (ML) models, Neural Networks (NN) and symbolic regression, are adopted to formulate the per-cycle evolution of plastic strains. Each provides, respectively, high expressiveness and explicit evolution equations. Both ML-based cycle-domain models achieve accurate predictions within and beyond the training regime. As a second approach, an NN-based explicit time integrator is formulated that is capable of taking large strain increments while maintaining accuracy and numerical robustness. The framework is physics-encoded, as it fulfills fundamental plasticity constraints by construction. Material point and finite element simulations demonstrate high accuracy, generalizability, and a considerable reduction in computational time.

article.lead: 钢轨表层在反复滚动接触中积累塑性变形，既改变材料的疲劳行为，也增加长期仿真的难度。这篇学位论文摘要围绕裂纹萌生预测与塑性计算加速展开，阅读价值在于同时关注“材料状态是否描述准确”和“计算是否足够高效”。

sections.title: 裂纹预测不能忽略已变形的钢轨表层
paragraphs: 滚动接触疲劳（RCF）裂纹萌生常与钢轨和车轮表层积累的大塑性变形有关。这些变形会影响材料的力学与疲劳行为，并诱发各向异性。摘要指出，许多相关研究未考虑近表层变形材料的影响，而长期交通载荷下的塑性累积仿真又需要较高计算成本。

sections.title: 把材料状态纳入预测，再加速循环塑性计算
paragraphs: 针对混合交通载荷下的轨头，研究利用类铁路载荷实验，标定对应不同轨头深度材料状态的各向异性模型；再根据现场样本测量重建累积剪应变分布，描述轨头材料性能的空间变化。预测框架同时关注轨头轮廓几何变化，并引入考虑累积塑性变形的改进裂纹萌生准则。
计算加速采用不同思路：循环域材料模型预测每个加载循环的峰值应力与塑性应变，并分别用神经网络和符号回归表达塑性应变的逐循环演化；另一种方法构建神经网络显式时间积分器，允许采用较大的应变增量，并通过结构设计满足基本塑性约束。

sections.title: 表层状态影响预测，机器学习支持计算提速
paragraphs: 摘要报告，预测RCF裂纹萌生时，考虑近表层变形材料及轨头轮廓几何变化具有重要意义。循环域方法中，神经网络提供较强表达能力，符号回归提供显式演化方程；两类模型在训练范围内及其之外均获得了准确预测。
对于神经网络显式时间积分器，摘要报告其在较大应变增量下保持准确性和数值稳健性。材料点与有限元仿真展示了较高精度、泛化能力和计算时间的显著减少，但摘要未给出具体误差或加速幅度。

sections.title: 摘要尚不足以界定验证边界
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断实验及现场样本的数量、材料与载荷覆盖范围，也无法确定比较基线、误差指标和计算耗时的测试条件。“训练范围之外”的具体跨度、裂纹萌生预测的验证方式，以及不同加速方法是否直接比较，仍需查阅正文；这些信息未在摘要中报告，不代表论文没有开展相关工作。

sections.title: 阅读启发：分别审视物理描述与加速边界
paragraphs: 阅读启发：面向疲劳可靠性与智能运维，可重点追问材料状态如何传递到裂纹萌生判据，以及机器学习加速在什么载荷和材料范围内有效。进一步阅读时，宜区分塑性响应预测准确与裂纹萌生预测准确这两个层次，不宜直接把仿真加速理解为已经验证了维护决策效果。

core.title: Digital Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance in Smart Manufacturing: Integrating Machine Learning for Intelligent Mechanical System Optimization
core.venue: Computer and Decision Making An International Journal
core.abstract: The significance of predictive maintenance in the context of smart manufacturing is rooted in the fact that unexpected machine downtimes impact productivity, maintenance planning, and asset utilization. This research proposes an explainable machine-learning approach to use operational measurements as a data-driven virtual condition layer to support operational decisions for digital-twin-based maintenance. The AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance dataset with 10 thousand observations was analysed with 6 non-leaky machine-condition predictors. Precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) was used as the main evaluation metric to compare the models optimized on the development data set and tested on an independent validation data set: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees and HistGradientBoosting. HistGradientBoosting was chosen and the locked-test PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, balanced accuracy and failure recall were 0.8242, 0.9750, 0.9031, and 0.8235 respectively. The most important predictors identified by the permutation importance were torque, air temperature, and tool wear. One layer focused on validation, that showed maintenance risk, brought together 48 out of 51 failures for the locked test in the Critical band. The framework shows how explainable machine learning can be used to assist in failure-risk prioritization, condition-based maintenance and intelligent mechanical-system optimisation without losing the human element or ‘leaking' the target.

core.title: A Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Analog-To-Digital Converter Design Automation
core.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
core.abstract: ADCs play an important role in converting information from the analog world to the digital one; with modern applications requiring higher resolutions, speed, and power efficiency, it has become very difficult to design them. Traditionally, the design of an ADC follows an iterative design process that includes stages like specification, behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, schematic simulation, layout, and post-layout verification, which is laborious and requires much designer expertise due to the consideration of process-voltage-temperature variations and yield. In this work, we perform a review of the latest advancements in the use of machine learning (ML) to tackle the challenges of ADC design in recent years, with systematic search from 2015 to 2026 in IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv. Rather than organizing the literature on different ML algorithms, this paper categorizes ML approaches such as regression, tree-based models, SVM, ANN, CNN, GNN, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and Bayesian optimization in ADC design stages such as behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, calibration of comparators and capacitor arrays, calibration of ADC, layout optimization, prediction of PVT/yield variations, and design space exploration. Comparative analysis includes the benefits provided by each technique such as speed and accuracy improvements, as well as their main drawbacks. Open challenges are then presented, including lack of data, poor generalization performance, low explainability, and the largely unexplored topic of co-optimization across multiple stages. Finally, future trends in the field are presented in terms of new directions such as generative AI, GNN-based layout optimization, physics-informed learning, digital twins, and human-AI collaborative design, as well as risks and potential problems such as manufacturability and IP in generative approaches

core.title: A Review of IoT-Based Machine Health Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance Using Machine Learning: Architectures, Algorithms, and Open Challenges
core.abstract: Unplanned equipment failure remains one of the most expensive problems in modern manufacturing, and the maintenance strategy adopted by a plant has a direct bearing on its productivity, safety, and operating cost. Traditional reactive and time-based preventive approaches either allow machines to run to failure or replace healthy components too early, and neither uses the rich stream of data that industrial assets now generate. The convergence of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and machine learning has made a third option practical: predictive maintenance, in which the condition of a machine is monitored continuously and its future health is estimated from sensor data. This paper reviews the state of the art in IoT-based machine health monitoring and machine-learning-driven predictive maintenance. We examine the layered sensing-to-cloud architectures that underpin such systems, survey the feature-extraction and learning methods that have been applied to fault classification and remaining-useful-life estimation, and compare representative studies spanning support vector machines, ensemble methods, deep networks, image-based diagnosis, and survival analysis. Reported accuracies range from roughly 88% for a single-classifier failure detector to 96% for a vision-based gearbox diagnostic, while survival models achieve concordance indices above 0.97 on real industrial data. Drawing these threads together, we identify a set of recurring gaps: an over-reliance on single algorithms and balanced benchmark datasets, the fragmented treatment of fault classification and life estimation, the limited adoption of survival analysis in an Industry 4.0 setting, and unresolved questions around edge deployment, security, and interpretability. We close by outlining an integrated research direction that unifies real-time IoT sensing with a combined classification-and-prognostics pipeline.

core.title: Machine learning-based inverse method for determining elastic coefficients of unsymmetric laminates
core.abstract: Determination of equivalent elastic coefficients in composite laminates is a fundamental problem in structural mechanics and materials engineering. This task becomes particularly challenging for unsymmetric laminates, where coupling effects between membrane, bending, and shear responses render analytical characterisation difficult and computationally expensive. In this work, a machine learning-based inverse methodology is proposed for determining the equivalent shear modulus of unsymmetric composite laminates. A high-fidelity finite element implementation of the ASTM V-notched shear test is used to generate a comprehensive dataset covering a wide range of unsymmetric stacking sequences. A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model is trained as a nonlinear surrogate to map laminate design variables to the corresponding equivalent shear modulus. The trained model is subsequently employed in an inverse design framework to identify laminate stacking sequences that achieve prescribed target values of shear modulus. The proposed approach significantly reduces computational cost compared to conventional trial-and-error finite element analysis and provides new insight into the relationship between laminate architecture and effective shear behaviour.

papers.title: Zero-Shot Open Circuit Fault Diagnosis of Converter Based on Prior-Knowledge Injected Dual Bayesian Network With Attention Mechanism
papers.venue: IEEE transactions on industrial electronics (1982. Print)
papers.abstract: Power electronic systems serve as core infrastructure for modern energy conversion and power control. Their reliability is crucial for the stable operation of key fields, such as industrial power systems, transportation, and aerospace. Open-circuit faults are difficult to detect, which can lead to serious consequences. While effective in data-rich environments, existing data-driven approaches’ reliance on extensive labeled data hinders their practical deployment. The reason is that acquiring comprehensive fault data in real-world settings is often prohibitively expensive. To address this, this article proposes a dual Bayesian zero-shot fault diagnosis approach based on prior-knowledge injected with attention mechanism (PKIDBAAM). This approach constructs a fault attribute space with clear physical meaning by analyzing the physical relationship between the Vienna rectifier topology and fault modes. It employs a multihead attention mechanism to dynamically fuse multidomain fault features from three-phase current signals. A dual Bayesian inference framework combining naive Bayes and integrated multiple Gaussian Bayesian algorithms is designed to achieve high accuracy recognition of inaccessible open-circuit faults. article.lead: 真实设备的开路故障数据昂贵且难以收集，依赖大量标注样本的诊断方法因此面临落地障碍。这项研究以Vienna整流器为对象，将物理先验、注意力机制与双贝叶斯推断结合，探索对难以获取数据的开路故障进行零样本诊断。

sections.title: 故障难采集，诊断不能只靠堆数据
paragraphs: 电力电子系统承担能量转换与功率控制，其可靠性关系到工业电力系统、交通运输和航空航天等领域的稳定运行。开路故障难以检测，而实际场景中获取全面故障数据的成本又很高，这使依赖大量标注数据的方法受到限制。
本文关注的核心问题是：当目标开路故障的数据难以获得时，能否利用电路自身的物理关系辅助识别，而不是完全依赖故障样本覆盖？摘要提出的零样本诊断方法，正是围绕这一数据瓶颈展开。

sections.title: 把物理属性、电流特征与贝叶斯推断结合
paragraphs: 作者提出融合先验知识与注意力机制的双贝叶斯零样本故障诊断方法，简称PKIDBAAM。方法首先分析Vienna整流器拓扑与故障模式之间的物理关系，据此构建具有明确物理意义的故障属性空间。
在信号侧，方法采用多头注意力机制，动态融合来自三相电流信号的多域故障特征；在推断侧，将朴素贝叶斯与集成多高斯贝叶斯算法结合，构成双贝叶斯推断框架，用于识别难以获取数据的开路故障。

sections.title: 实验平台报告优于经典机器学习模型
paragraphs: 摘要报告，研究在Vienna整流器实验平台上进行了验证，结果显著优于常规经典机器学习模型。这为所提方法在该平台上的故障诊断能力提供了支持，但摘要没有给出准确率、性能差值或具体对比模型，不能据此量化优势大小。

sections.title: 零样本划分与验证边界仍需查阅正文
paragraphs: 仅凭摘要，无法判断实验样本规模、故障类别覆盖、已见与未见故障的划分，以及训练和测试数据如何组织；也无法核对比较模型的配置、评价指标与“显著优于”的统计依据。这些属于当前资料未报告的信息，不意味着论文没有开展相应工作。

sections.title: 阅读启发：关注物理属性如何连接未见故障
paragraphs: 阅读启发：这项工作的值得关注之处，是把具有物理意义的故障属性引入数据受限的诊断问题。进一步阅读时，可重点追问属性空间如何连接已见与未见故障、多头注意力与双贝叶斯推断各自发挥什么作用，以及实验如何界定零样本识别。厘清这些问题，比仅关注总体性能更有助于判断其智能运维价值。

papers.title: Predicting crack initiation in highly deformed rail steel; Plasticity modeling, machine-learning-accelerated plasticity simulations, and fatigue criteria
papers.abstract: Rolling Contact Fatigue (RCF) crack initiation, causing major problems for the railway industry, is often associated with large plastic deformations accumulated in the surface layer of rails and wheels. These deformations are known to affect the mechanical and fatigue behavior of the material and to induce anisotropy. Even so, many RCF crack initiation studies do not account for the influence of the deformed near-surface material. Moreover, numerical simulations of the long-term accumulation of plastic deformations under traffic loading are computationally demanding. To address these challenges, the goal of this thesis is to develop methodologies for both more accurate predictions of RCF crack initiation in the highly deformed near-surface rail material and computationally efficient modeling of plasticity.In the first part of the thesis, a framework is developed for predicting RCF crack initiation in railheads subjected to mixed traffic loading, with a focus on the effects of the highly deformed rail surface layer and profile geometry changes. In particular, an anisotropic material model is calibrated against experiments with railway-like loading at different material states, corresponding to different depths in the railhead. The identified material parameters are then used to consider spatially varying properties in the railhead, governed by an accumulated shear strain distribution reconstructed from measurements in field samples. The framework further incorporates an improved crack initiation criterion that accounts for the accumulated plastic deformations. The findings underline the significant importance of accounting for the deformed near-surface material and rail profile geometry changes when predicting RCF crack initiation.The second part of the thesis presents two approaches to reducing the computational cost of cyclic plasticity simulations. First, a cycle-domain material model is used to predict peak stress and plastic strain in each loading cycle. Machine Learning (ML) models, Neural Networks (NN) and symbolic regression, are adopted to formulate the per-cycle evolution of plastic strains. Each provides, respectively, high expressiveness and explicit evolution equations. Both ML-based cycle-domain models achieve accurate predictions within and beyond the training regime. As a second approach, an NN-based explicit time integrator is formulated that is capable of taking large strain increments while maintaining accuracy and numerical robustness. The framework is physics-encoded, as it fulfills fundamental plasticity constraints by construction. Material point and finite element simulations demonstrate high accuracy, generalizability, and a considerable reduction in computational time.

papers.title: Digital Twin-Driven Predictive Maintenance in Smart Manufacturing: Integrating Machine Learning for Intelligent Mechanical System Optimization
papers.venue: Computer and Decision Making An International Journal
papers.abstract: The significance of predictive maintenance in the context of smart manufacturing is rooted in the fact that unexpected machine downtimes impact productivity, maintenance planning, and asset utilization. This research proposes an explainable machine-learning approach to use operational measurements as a data-driven virtual condition layer to support operational decisions for digital-twin-based maintenance. The AI4I 2020 Predictive Maintenance dataset with 10 thousand observations was analysed with 6 non-leaky machine-condition predictors. Precision-recall area under the curve (PR-AUC) was used as the main evaluation metric to compare the models optimized on the development data set and tested on an independent validation data set: Logistic Regression, Random Forest, Extra Trees and HistGradientBoosting. HistGradientBoosting was chosen and the locked-test PR-AUC, ROC-AUC, balanced accuracy and failure recall were 0.8242, 0.9750, 0.9031, and 0.8235 respectively. The most important predictors identified by the permutation importance were torque, air temperature, and tool wear. One layer focused on validation, that showed maintenance risk, brought together 48 out of 51 failures for the locked test in the Critical band. The framework shows how explainable machine learning can be used to assist in failure-risk prioritization, condition-based maintenance and intelligent mechanical-system optimisation without losing the human element or ‘leaking' the target.

papers.title: A Review of Machine Learning Techniques for Analog-To-Digital Converter Design Automation
papers.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
papers.abstract: ADCs play an important role in converting information from the analog world to the digital one; with modern applications requiring higher resolutions, speed, and power efficiency, it has become very difficult to design them. Traditionally, the design of an ADC follows an iterative design process that includes stages like specification, behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, schematic simulation, layout, and post-layout verification, which is laborious and requires much designer expertise due to the consideration of process-voltage-temperature variations and yield. In this work, we perform a review of the latest advancements in the use of machine learning (ML) to tackle the challenges of ADC design in recent years, with systematic search from 2015 to 2026 in IEEE Xplore, ACM Digital Library, and arXiv. Rather than organizing the literature on different ML algorithms, this paper categorizes ML approaches such as regression, tree-based models, SVM, ANN, CNN, GNN, reinforcement learning, evolutionary algorithms, and Bayesian optimization in ADC design stages such as behavioral modeling, transistor sizing, calibration of comparators and capacitor arrays, calibration of ADC, layout optimization, prediction of PVT/yield variations, and design space exploration. Comparative analysis includes the benefits provided by each technique such as speed and accuracy improvements, as well as their main drawbacks. Open challenges are then presented, including lack of data, poor generalization performance, low explainability, and the largely unexplored topic of co-optimization across multiple stages. Finally, future trends in the field are presented in terms of new directions such as generative AI, GNN-based layout optimization, physics-informed learning, digital twins, and human-AI collaborative design, as well as risks and potential problems such as manufacturability and IP in generative approaches

papers.title: A Review of IoT-Based Machine Health Monitoring and Predictive Maintenance Using Machine Learning: Architectures, Algorithms, and Open Challenges
papers.abstract: Unplanned equipment failure remains one of the most expensive problems in modern manufacturing, and the maintenance strategy adopted by a plant has a direct bearing on its productivity, safety, and operating cost. Traditional reactive and time-based preventive approaches either allow machines to run to failure or replace healthy components too early, and neither uses the rich stream of data that industrial assets now generate. The convergence of the Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) and machine learning has made a third option practical: predictive maintenance, in which the condition of a machine is monitored continuously and its future health is estimated from sensor data. This paper reviews the state of the art in IoT-based machine health monitoring and machine-learning-driven predictive maintenance. We examine the layered sensing-to-cloud architectures that underpin such systems, survey the feature-extraction and learning methods that have been applied to fault classification and remaining-useful-life estimation, and compare representative studies spanning support vector machines, ensemble methods, deep networks, image-based diagnosis, and survival analysis. Reported accuracies range from roughly 88% for a single-classifier failure detector to 96% for a vision-based gearbox diagnostic, while survival models achieve concordance indices above 0.97 on real industrial data. Drawing these threads together, we identify a set of recurring gaps: an over-reliance on single algorithms and balanced benchmark datasets, the fragmented treatment of fault classification and life estimation, the limited adoption of survival analysis in an Industry 4.0 setting, and unresolved questions around edge deployment, security, and interpretability. We close by outlining an integrated research direction that unifies real-time IoT sensing with a combined classification-and-prognostics pipeline.

papers.title: Machine learning-based inverse method for determining elastic coefficients of unsymmetric laminates
papers.abstract: Determination of equivalent elastic coefficients in composite laminates is a fundamental problem in structural mechanics and materials engineering. This task becomes particularly challenging for unsymmetric laminates, where coupling effects between membrane, bending, and shear responses render analytical characterisation difficult and computationally expensive. In this work, a machine learning-based inverse methodology is proposed for determining the equivalent shear modulus of unsymmetric composite laminates. A high-fidelity finite element implementation of the ASTM V-notched shear test is used to generate a comprehensive dataset covering a wide range of unsymmetric stacking sequences. A Light Gradient Boosting Machine (LightGBM) model is trained as a nonlinear surrogate to map laminate design variables to the corresponding equivalent shear modulus. The trained model is subsequently employed in an inverse design framework to identify laminate stacking sequences that achieve prescribed target values of shear modulus. The proposed approach significantly reduces computational cost compared to conventional trial-and-error finite element analysis and provides new insight into the relationship between laminate architecture and effective shear behaviour.
